citation: CoptOT: The Sahidic Old Testament. Coptic SCRIPTORIUM, KELLIA, version 6.1 (2025). CC BY-SA 4.0.
editorialMarkers: The Coptic Old Testament follows the Septuagint (Greek) order and wording; chapter and verse numbers are the corpus’s and may not match the Hebrew. Segmentation and tagging are automatic; Greek loanwords are marked by the corpus. Where this witness does not carry a verse — Acts 8:37 and Mark 9:46 among them, verses absent from most early manuscripts — the edition marks the place rather than dropping the verse, and Wellspring writes every such mark the same way, as “[—]”, so that the gap is visible and the numbering stays true. That marker is the edition’s own and is reproduced here unchanged: it means the verse is not in this manuscript tradition, not that the text is unknown.
method: Verse text is the corpus’s bound groups (orig_group / <phr>) joined with spaces; loanwords the corpus marks as Greek, Hebrew or Latin are kept as spans (sp.loan) for Word study; no normalisation of spelling.
